arguments.value:
Go Call and PageMaster agreed to run a joint promotion offering free Motorola alphanumeric pagers with no activation fee to customers who signed up for 12 months of numeric paging service and prepaid airtime. Customers had to pay monthly airtime charges, shipping and handling, and taxes, and the airtime was nonrefundable. The promotion ran from June 1, 1999 to June 1, 2000, with a possible one-year extension if enough pagers were distributed.

PageMaster was responsible for the toll-free ordering line, supplying pagers, fulfillment, delivery, handling defects and customer complaints, contracting with the airtime provider, and providing software for Go Call to send short messages to promotion customers. PageMaster also agreed not to run a similar promotion with other online casinos during the term. Go Call was responsible for creating and paying for advertising, getting PageMaster’s prior approval of all ad materials, and not doing a similar promotion with other paging companies during the term.

Go Call had to pay a $100,000 refundable deposit to secure pager inventory, and PageMaster would refund $1 per pager delivered, up to the full deposit, with monthly accounting and audit rights for Go Call. PageMaster also agreed to pay Go Call co-op marketing funds of $3 per pager and 5% of airtime renewal revenue.

The agreement includes trademark approval and indemnity rules, limits on liability, force majeure protection, California law and Los Angeles venue, and a requirement that disputes first go through negotiation and then binding arbitration if unresolved. The agreement also requires confidentiality, gives notice procedures, and says it would expire if not properly signed and delivered by March 26, 1999.
